key_facts: Root package.json (pi/package.json:1) devDependencies only (no root prod deps); workspaces=[packages/*, packages/session-backends/*, plus 5 example-extension dirs incl. packages/coding-agent/examples/extensions/gondolin] — that gondolin example pulls ssh2/cpu-features into a full monorepo dev install but NOT into the published CLI.

Direct PRODUCTION deps per package.json: pi-tui=2 external (get-east-asian-width 1.6.0, marked 18.0.5), 0 internal — lightest package. pi-agent-core=4 external (diff 8.0.4, ignore 7.0.5, typebox 1.3.7, yaml 2.9.0) + 2 internal. pi-ai=11 external (@anthropic-ai/sdk 0.91.1, @aws-sdk/client-bedrock-runtime 3.1048.0, @google/genai 1.52.0, @mistralai/mistralai 2.2.6, @opentelemetry/api 1.9.0, @smithy/node-http-handler 4.7.3, http-proxy-agent 7.0.2, https-proxy-agent 7.0.6, openai 6.26.0, partial-json 0.1.7, typebox 1.3.7) + 1 internal. pi-coding-agent (packages/coding-agent/package.json:45-77)=15 external (@silvia-odwyer/photon-node 0.3.4, chalk, cross-spawn, diff, glob, grok-mermaid 0.2.2, highlight.js, hosted-git-info, ignore, jiti, minimatch, proper-lockfile, semver, typebox, undici, yaml) + 5 internal + 1 optional (@mariozechner/clipboard 0.3.9). pi-protocol=1 (typebox). pi-client/pi-server/pi-telemetry/pi-evals/session-backends/sqlite-node=0 external prod deps (sqlite-node uses Node's built-in node:sqlite, no native binding).

Transitive counts (measured, not estimated): real `npm ci --ignore-scripts` at repo root installed 339 packages total; `npm ls --all --omit=dev --parseable` across all workspaces = 167 production-reachable entries; `npm ls --all --parseable` (incl. dev) = 340; lockfile packages map has 429 total entries / 414 node_modules entries / 386 unique names, of which 235 are dev-only. The actual npm-published @earendil-works/pi-coding-agent tree (via its generated npm-shrinkwrap.json) is only 143 packages (142 unique + itself) — materially smaller than the full monorepo dev graph.

Lifecycle scripts (from real lockfile hasInstallScript=true, 7 total): @google/genai@1.52.0 (prod, in pi-ai) preinstall='echo no-op' (verified harmless); protobufjs@7.6.5 (prod, transitive of @google/genai, pinned via root overrides at package.json:65-70 and coding-agent/package.json:68-73) postinstall runs scripts/postinstall.js which only prints a version-scheme mismatch warning (verified harmless, read source); cpu-features@0.0.10 and ssh2@1.17.0 (dev-graph only, pulled solely by the gondolin example-extension workspace, install.js/node-gyp compiles native code) — NOT in the shipped coding-agent shrinkwrap; canvas@3.2.3 (devDependency of packages/ai for tests) runs prebuild-install/node-gyp; esbuild@0.28.1 and fsevents@2.3.3 are devDeps with install scripts but ship prebuilt platform binaries via optionalDependencies.

The coding-agent shrinkwrap generator (scripts/generate-coding-agent-shrinkwrap.mjs:13-16) hard-codes an allowlist of exactly 2 packages permitted to have install scripts in the published artifact: @google/genai@1.52.0 and protobufjs@7.6.5, each with a written justification comment; the validator (lines 241-254) fails the build if ANY other package in the resolved tree has hasInstallScript=true, and separately fails if a previously-allowlisted package disappears (stale-allowlist detection, lines 257-261). Confirmed by inspecting the generated packages/coding-agent/npm-shrinkwrap.json: exactly those 2 packages (of 143) have hasInstallScript.

`npm install --ignore-scripts` DOES protect the build in practice: after a real `npm ci --ignore-scripts --no-audit --no-fund` (9s, 339 packages), `node node_modules/esbuild/bin/esbuild --version` ran successfully (0.28.1) because the platform binary ships via the @esbuild/linux-x64 optionalDependency, not via the skipped postinstall. The two prod packages with install scripts were independently verified to be no-ops/warn-only, so skipping their scripts loses no needed functionality either.

Root .npmrc (pi/.npmrc:1-2): `save-exact=true` (forces exact pins on every `npm install <pkg>`) and `min-release-age=2`. VERIFIED LIVE (not just documented): running `npm config list` inside the repo shows npm 11.12.1 dynamically translating this into `before = "<now minus exactly 2 days>"` (measured: real UTC time 2026-08-07T00:16:38Z -> before=2026-08-05T00:16:38.268Z, to the second) — i.e. npm's install resolver actively refuses any dependency version published within the last 2 days, a real mitigation against fast-propagating npm account-takeover/worm attacks (e.g. Shai-Hulud-style 2025 incidents).

scripts/check-pinned-deps.mjs (pi/scripts/check-pinned-deps.mjs:1-63, run via `npm run check`) walks every package.json in the repo and fails CI/pre-commit if any external (non `@earendil-works/pi-*`, non workspace:/file:/git:/http(s):) dependency in dependencies/devDependencies/optionalDependencies is not an exact X.Y.Z semver (regex line 5) — guarantees no `^`/`~`/range specifiers for direct deps anywhere in the monorepo. It does NOT touch transitive pinning (that's package-lock.json's job) and does not verify integrity/signatures itself.

scripts/generate-coding-agent-shrinkwrap.mjs (pi/scripts/generate-coding-agent-shrinkwrap.mjs) computes the coding-agent's full transitive closure purely from package.json graphs + the root package-lock.json (no node_modules needed), writes packages/coding-agent/npm-shrinkwrap.json (shipped in the published npm tarball per `files` in packages/coding-agent/package.json:27-34) with resolved tarball URLs + sha512 integrity per package (copied straight from the lockfile). Because npm-shrinkwrap.json (unlike package-lock.json) is honored by npm when a consumer runs `npm install @earendil-works/pi-coding-agent`, this pins the exact transitive tree + integrity hashes for END USERS of the published CLI, not just contributors in this repo. `npm run check:shrinkwrap` (--check mode) fails CI if the checked-in file is stale vs. the lockfile.

scripts/generate-coding-agent-install-lock.mjs (pi/scripts/generate-coding-agent-install-lock.mjs) produces a separate standalone install root at packages/coding-agent/install-lock/{package.json,package-lock.json} for a synthetic private package @earendil-works/pi-coding-agent-install whose only dependency is the exact-pinned coding-agent version; used by pi's self-updater/local-release tooling (README.md:86: '...`pi update --self` use `--ignore-scripts` where supported') to do a fully pre-resolved install without invoking npm's registry resolver at all. No references to it were found in packages/coding-agent/src (it's an external-tooling artifact, not something the running CLI reads).

SECURITY.md (pi/SECURITY.md:42-68) explicitly scopes OUT: local code execution/lack of sandbox, extension/skill behavior, untrusted-repo risk, installing untrusted packages/extensions, prompt injection, and any report requiring prior local write access to `~/.pi` etc. It scopes IN dependency reports only if they show the shipped dependency is affected AND reachable through Pi (SECURITY.md:85-86) — i.e. upstream will not treat 'has a vulnerable devDependency' as a valid report; that burden falls on strape's own audit process.

packages/coding-agent/docs/security.md documents Project Trust (.pi/settings.json, .pi/extensions, .pi/skills etc. require an interactive trust prompt, default `defaultProjectTrust: "ask"`, decisions cached in ~/.pi/agent/trust.json) but states plainly there is 'No Built-in Sandbox' (line 31) and that context files (AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md) load regardless of trust (line 27) — i.e. trust gates extensions/skills but not context-file prompt injection.

CI evidence: .github/workflows/npm-audit.yml runs daily (cron) `npm ci --ignore-scripts --no-audit --no-fund` then `npm audit --omit=dev --audit-level=moderate` then `npm audit signatures --omit=dev`. .github/workflows/ci.yml runs `npm ci --ignore-scripts` on every push/PR to main. Both pin `actions/checkout` and `actions/setup-node` by full commit SHA (with version comment), not by mutable tag — a supply-chain hardening detail on the Actions side too. No Dependabot/Renovate config exists anywhere in the repo (grep found none) — dependency bumps are manual/reviewed only, consistent with README's stated 'we treat npm dependency changes as reviewed code changes.'

Live `npm audit --package-lock-only --omit=dev` and (incl. dev) both returned 'found 0 vulnerabilities' when actually run against the registry (network access WAS available in this environment, contradicting the task's 'note if offline' caveat — npm ping succeeded, 237ms). After a real `npm ci` install, `npm audit signatures` (which needs real node_modules, not just the lockfile — it failed with '--package-lock-only') reported: audited 324 packages, ALL 324 have verified registry signatures, and 66 have verified npm provenance/sigstore attestations.

.husky/pre-commit (pi/.husky/pre-commit) runs scripts/check-lockfile-commit.mjs before every commit: if package-lock.json is staged and the diff touches any node_modules/* entries (not just internal workspace metadata), the commit is BLOCKED with a printed summary of every added/removed/changed package, unless `PI_ALLOW_LOCKFILE_CHANGE=1` is set. This is exactly the 'dependency review gate that diffs the lockfile and forces review of new/changed deps' the user wants for upstream syncs, and it already exists upstream — strape can reuse it verbatim for reviewing lockfile diffs when merging future pi releases.

Root package.json `overrides` (pi/package.json:65-70, duplicated in packages/coding-agent/package.json:68-73) pins protobufjs to exact 7.6.5 and rimraf to exact 6.1.2 (incl. nested override for gaxios>rimraf) across the whole graph even though upstream packages request looser ranges (e.g. lockfile shows a dependent requesting protobufjs ^7.5.4) — prevents a transitive floating range from silently resolving to an unreviewed newer/older version.

Riskiest DIRECT prod dependencies by concrete trust signals (not just presence of install scripts): grok-mermaid@0.2.2 (packages/coding-agent/package.json:56) is a brand-new, essentially unvetted package — npm registry data shows it was created 2026-07-28 (created key), the pinned 0.2.2 was published 2026-08-04 (only ~2 days before the observed 'now'), it has a single maintainer (xl0), and only 1,239 npm downloads in the trailing 30 days (per api.npmjs.org/downloads). It has zero dependencies and no install script, but by every other supply-chain heuristic (age, maintainer count, popularity) it is the single weakest link in the shipped dependency graph. proper-lockfile@4.1.2 (used for session-file locking) has not been published since 2022-06-24 (unmaintained/abandoned upstream, though widely used: 84.4M monthly downloads). @silvia-odwyer/photon-node@0.3.4 (WASM image resize, single maintainer) last published 2025-05-10.

@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent's `piConfig.configDir` is `.pi` (packages/coding-agent/package.json:6-8) — confirms CONFIG_DIR_NAME resolves to `.pi`, relevant to the separate CLAUDE.md/.claude reuse goal, not to this security task directly.
risks: strape will inherit whatever it forks: if strape vendors the full monorepo (incl. example-extension workspaces like gondolin/sandbox) as its dev tree, ssh2 + cpu-features (both native, install scripts that compile via node-gyp or fetch prebuilt binaries over the network) enter the local dev/build supply-chain surface even though they never ship in the coding-agent npm package — a naive 'npm install' of the whole repo without pruning those example workspaces widens strape's attack surface unnecessarily for a project that has no need for the gondolin micro-VM sandbox extension.

The npm-shrinkwrap.json / install-lock generation scripts are 'trust but verify' tooling: they are only as good as the human review at the point a new install-script package is added to allowedInstallScriptPackages (currently 2 entries, each with a one-line justification that was NOT independently re-verified by an automated check beyond string-matching the postinstall file didn't change — a maintainer typo or a compromised protobufjs@7.6.5 republish with the same version+script name would not be re-flagged unless the integrity hash in the lockfile also changed, which it would, but the check script does not diff script *contents*, only presence/allowlist membership).

grok-mermaid is a real, current (as of the audit date) concrete risk: a single-maintainer, ~1-week-old, low-download npm package is a direct production dependency of the published CLI. If strape keeps this dependency via upstream sync, a compromise of that one maintainer's npm account (or a malicious later version silently satisfying the exact-pin only until the next routine bump) is a plausible attack path that none of pi's existing automation (pinned-deps check, shrinkwrap, npm audit, signatures) would catch, because it has no known CVE, no install script, and a valid registry signature — those controls only catch known-vuln/script/unsigned-package classes of risk, not 'young/thin-trust package' risk.

SECURITY.md explicitly puts 'dependency reports that are not reachable/shipped' and general local-agent behavior out of scope for upstream's bug bounty — meaning strape cannot rely on upstream pi's security process to surface or fix dependency risk in packages strape doesn't directly control; strape must run its own recurring dependency-risk scanning (OSV/Socket-style) rather than assuming upstream's daily npm-audit workflow covers everything the user cares about (it only covers known-CVE + missing-signature classes).

`npm audit signatures` (registry-signature + provenance verification) requires a real `node_modules` install to run — a pure lockfile-only, no-install CI/audit step (as the task literally proposed: 'npm audit --package-lock-only') CANNOT verify signatures/provenance; it can only check known-CVEs. If strape builds a hardening pipeline that stays lockfile-only for speed, it will silently lose signature/provenance verification coverage unless it also runs a real install step (as pi's own npm-audit.yml correctly does).

No Dependabot/Renovate or scheduled dependency-freshness bot exists upstream; combined with `min-release-age=2` (only 2 days) and manual-only bumps, there is no forcing function to routinely re-review or age-gate dependencies beyond 2 days — a slow-burn attack (a version that looks fine for the first 2+ days) is not defended against by this specific control, only truly fast worm-style propagation is.
recommendations: Reuse pi's supply-chain tooling as-is when forking to strape rather than rebuilding: keep .npmrc (save-exact=true, min-release-age=2 — verified live-functioning, translates to a dynamic `before` cutoff), scripts/check-pinned-deps.mjs, scripts/generate-coding-agent-shrinkwrap.mjs (rename target to a strape-coding-agent shrinkwrap), scripts/generate-coding-agent-install-lock.mjs, scripts/check-lockfile-commit.mjs + the .husky/pre-commit wiring, and the .github/workflows/npm-audit.yml + ci.yml patterns (both already use `--ignore-scripts` and SHA-pinned Actions). This is the 'minimum effort, best quality' path per the user's stated optimization goal — these scripts are generic enough to work unmodified against a renamed/forked lockfile.

Because the goal is Grok+OpenAI only (no Anthropic models), strip @anthropic-ai/sdk from packages/ai's dependencies and the example extension packages/coding-agent/examples/extensions/custom-provider-anthropic from the root workspaces array; also drop @aws-sdk/client-bedrock-runtime, @google/genai (and its install-script + protobufjs override), @mistralai/mistralai if those provider integrations are unused by strape — this directly shrinks the transitive graph (measured at 167 prod / 340 total packages for the full monorepo) and removes protobufjs's install script entirely, reducing the shrinkwrap's install-script allowlist from 2 entries to potentially 0.

Exclude devDependency-only example/sandbox workspaces the user doesn't need (packages/coding-agent/examples/extensions/gondolin and .../sandbox, which pull in ssh2, cpu-features, canvas — all native/install-script packages) from strape's root package.json `workspaces` array, or delete those example directories outright, so `npm ci` never touches ssh2/cpu-features/canvas in strape's dev environment at all (they are already absent from the shipped coding-agent shrinkwrap, so removing them is purely an upstream-sync/dev-supply-chain cleanup, zero functional loss).

Explicitly flag grok-mermaid (packages/coding-agent/package.json:56) for a manual security review before strape's first build: read its full source (it's tiny — Mermaid-to-Unicode renderer, zero deps), consider vendoring/inlining the ~1 file it needs instead of depending on a single-maintainer week-old npm package, or at minimum pin+monitor it specifically (e.g., add it to a 'high-scrutiny' list that requires re-review on every version bump, not just relying on min-release-age/exact-pin).

Add a real dependency-scanning layer beyond what upstream has, since upstream's npm-audit.yml only catches known-CVEs + missing signatures: integrate `osv-scanner` (or Socket.dev / `npq`) as a CI job and as a pre-merge gate specifically on package-lock.json diffs, so 'young package / single maintainer / low downloads / recently transferred ownership' heuristics (the class of risk that caught grok-mermaid above) are surfaced automatically rather than requiring manual npm-registry lookups like the ones done in this audit.

For the upstream-sync workflow (goal #5, maintainability): treat scripts/check-lockfile-commit.mjs's existing behavior as strape's dependency-review gate for every `git merge upstream/main` — run `git diff <last-synced-sha> HEAD -- package-lock.json` and require the same 'added/removed/changed package' review before accepting the merge, exactly as the pre-commit hook already enforces for local commits. Because this script already prints a clean summary and only requires a diff of two package-lock.json blobs, it needs no changes to work for periodic upstream merges, not just local commits.

Generate a CycloneDX SBOM (`npx @cyclonedx/cyclonedx-npm --output-format json`) from the resolved lockfile as part of strape's release process and diff it release-over-release; combine with `npm audit signatures` (which requires a real install, unlike `--package-lock-only`) in CI so provenance/attestation coverage (66/324 packages currently have verified attestations per this audit) is tracked over time and regressions (a previously-attested package losing attestation) are caught.

Given the user's stated preference for maximum security with minimum effort, do NOT stand up a full offline verdaccio mirror or vendor tarballs initially — the existing controls (exact pins, shrinkwrap with integrity hashes, --ignore-scripts everywhere, min-release-age, daily audit+signatures) already cover the highest-value, lowest-effort wins. Reserve vendoring/offline-mirror investment for if/when strape needs air-gapped or high-assurance builds; until then, prioritize the cheap wins above (trim unused providers/examples, scan grok-mermaid, add osv-scanner, reuse the lockfile-diff gate for upstream syncs).

Verify (do not assume) that `--ignore-scripts` preserves functionality for any NEW dependency strape adds, the same way this audit empirically confirmed esbuild's prebuilt binary still works and @google/genai/protobufjs's scripts are no-ops/warn-only — add a one-line CI smoke step (e.g. run the built CLI's `--version`/`--help`) after an `--ignore-scripts` install so a future dependency that silently needs its postinstall (e.g. a real native compile) is caught immediately rather than discovered at runtime by a user.
summary: Pi's supply-chain posture is materially stronger than a typical npm monorepo: direct deps are exact-pinned and enforced by CI (scripts/check-pinned-deps.mjs), the published @earendil-works/pi-coding-agent package ships a generated npm-shrinkwrap.json (143 packages) with an explicit, validated allowlist of only 2 install-script packages (@google/genai, protobufjs — both verified harmless), all installs use --ignore-scripts (verified this doesn't break functionality), .npmrc's min-release-age=2 was empirically confirmed live (translates to a dynamic `before = now-2days` cutoff in npm 11.12.1), and a pre-commit hook (scripts/check-lockfile-commit.mjs) already implements exactly the "diff lockfile, review new/changed deps" gate the user wants for upstream syncs. Live npm audit (network was available) found 0 known vulnerabilities and 324/324 verified registry signatures with 66 provenance attestations. The one concrete risk this audit surfaces that none of pi's existing automation would catch is grok-mermaid@0.2.2, a direct production dependency that is a brand-new (created 2026-07-28), single-maintainer, ~1,239-monthly-download package — a "thin trust" supply-chain risk class (not CVE/signature-based) that warrants manual review or an osv-scanner/Socket-style CI gate before strape's first build.
